description: Document classes whose typed fields ontology/document_fields.py reads from captured document bytes (mail attachments, SharePoint files). A class is recognised by a title cue that starts a line; a field by one of its labels starting a line or a column (after a tab or two spaces) followed by ':', '#', a tab or two spaces. Vocabulary only: no case value belongs here. A new class is a new profile, not new code. The profile is the one declaration of its object_type's field properties: ontology/schema.py derives one property per field for every documentFields binding of that type (named by the field or its property key; a text field's identifier_kind makes it an identifier, a quantity field names its quantity_role, or count: true for a count of a unit that is no stock quantity (a decimal with its unit), an optional description is prepended), and refuses a hand-written one. A keyed field (keyed: a pattern of keys) reads one value per key written before it on the labelled line (entries separated by ';'), never a total. attests: which fields a document class states about an attested record type, compared at read time by plx.object (operating/ontology_tools.py) and reported as conflicts, never resolved; money only in one stated currency (never converted) and on one declared tax basis (a money field's tax_basis: incl_tax, excl_tax or tax_only when its labels state it; omitted is unknown, never compared, a gap), a record read from Business Central alone (no Portal row) at lead tier with its BC company named. A checkbox field (kind checkbox) reads one printed box: a mark of checkbox_marks.checked written after its label (label, optional ':' or '#', mark) or before it at a line or column start ('[x] Shipment released') is the value checked; a mark of checkbox_marks.unchecked is the gap unchecked (a blank box says nothing: never no, never zero); no mark or any other mark is the gap unreadable (the default: OCR loses and invents box glyphs). A checked mark is a box or a glyph, never a letter: a lone 'x' is OCR noise as often as a mark and reads unreadable, so no letter belongs in checkbox_marks.checked. A label with a box on both sides is unreadable (which box is the label's is unknown). A title_alone class's title cue fills its line or column ('Purchase Order', never 'Purchase Order No: 4500'), or is the label of its own number ('Purchase Order: 4500', a numbered title: no class beside another class's title line). number_field names the field holding a class's own document number: a whole-line title of a class whose number the document never states is a heading below a title of a class whose number it states, never a second class. line_items: a table whose header line names two or more columns by their labels (cells split by a tab, two spaces or Markdown pipes); each following line with as many cells is one item, every cell typed by its column's kind and cited by its own span (a bare quantity takes the unit_from cell as its unit; a per_unit_of price without its own unit is per that row's quantity unit). A table may be all text columns (a test table: a result is 'Conforms' as often as a number); a blank cell, or one with an unclear digit ('0.0?'), is that cell's gap. A compare rule may name the owner-system proposal type (propose, operating/action_catalog.json) through which a value the record holds empty may be proposed: operating/attested_conflicts.py reports it as a missing_in_record lead, never a write. A field may declare a marking of the schema's marking vocabulary (pii, finance, l5, purchasing_prices, quality_controlled; money is finance, unless the field declares a money marking every finance holder holds, ontology/store_ddl.py MARKING_HELD_WITH, which replaces it: purchasing_prices on a supplier's confirmed prices, overrides/markings.json scoped_markings): its property carries it, and so does the type's evidence property, which holds every field's value. A text field may declare refers_to, an identifier kind (ontology/schema/identifiers.json): its value is read as a reference of that kind and linked to the record holding it as a lead mention (the type must declare a mention link to the kind's object type), never as an identifier of the document. A profile's noun names the document in its derived descriptions (default: its object type in words). own_parties names PLX as it writes itself; a profile's not_issued_by_own_party (issuer_fields, recipient_fields, recipient_lines, own_record) makes a document PLX issued not of that class: its issuing party is an own party (an issuer field or, when none is stated, the unlabelled letterhead text before the title and before a recipient line or a label with no value: a line starting with a recipient_lines word names the addressee, never the issuer, and a labelled value is no letterhead; and no recipient field), or its provenance says so (a confirmed Portal DocumentCategory of an issued purchase order, or a mail attachment sent by the captured mailbox itself, unless a captured mailbox received the same bytes from outside: a forward or reply keeps the document's direction); without such a signal the class records the gap issuer_unknown, and plx.object reports the document as issued_by_own_party to a reader who may see an own record (own_record: the identifier kind, read from that field as the identifier grammar reads it) holding its number. code_synonyms folds a vocabulary's synonyms into one code ('CFR (CNF)' is one Incoterm). One scanner reads every table: a header line whose every cell is a line_items column label heads a line-items table, else one naming a field's cell column after its first cell heads a cell table, so no cell is read twice. A field's cell (rows: row labels, columns: column headers) also reads it from a table that states it per row (a shop-floor sheet's Filling and Total rows under QTY (EA)): below a header line naming one of its columns, a row whose first cell is one of its row labels gives that column's cell, cited by its own span, one more read of the field (two rows with two values conflict, never add up); such a row with another number of cells than its header is the gap unaligned, except on a layout page (OCR text rebuilt from word boxes, columns kept by position, its last line the layout mark; OCR text without the mark keeps the cell count rule), where a row cell lying under that header cell alone is read. A quantity stated in several units at once ('1509EA; 378CS') reads in the field's default_unit and keeps the others as alternates; conflicts are judged within one unit. A field the document never names (none of its labels or row labels starting a cell) is the gap not_stated; one it names where no value was read is label_seen_unread (a reader limit, never the document's silence) with its sub-reason unread: header_unseen, row_unaligned, single_spaced, no_key, handwritten_unkeyed or value_unplaced. A keyed box (part codes) reads blank (value_missing) only when nothing but its printed parenthetical or a fill line follows its label before a known label or heading; any other text there with no key read is label_seen_unread (no_key), never blank; on a word-box layout page whose mark line names at least 3/4 of that text (its words' characters) as read below the OCR handwriting bound it is handwritten_unkeyed instead (handwritten part codes OCR cannot key, citing the box text).

currencies.description: The labels a document declares its currency under. What a written currency is (ISO 4217 code, sign form, ambiguous sign) is the one table in ontology/units.py (currency_reading), shared with the document price reader.

own_parties.description: Names PLX (Petra) writes as itself on the documents it issues: the letterhead of its purchase-order PDF (plx-customer-portal@549f6f0 portal/src/app/mrp/purchase-orders/[id]/print/po-print-template.tsx) and its Business Central company names (ontology/schema/domains/bc_finance.json). Matched as whole words, case-insensitively.

stop_labels.description: Labels a document writes that no class reads a field from: contact and table-header words. Like a field label (starting a line, a column or following a space, then ':' or '#') one ends the value before it ('Supplier: Acme Co. Phone: ...' reads 'Acme Co.'); a value that is itself a declared label (a field's or one of these) is no value, and a row of declared labels alone is a header row with no value beside any of them. An undeclared word stays in the value. Vocabulary only: no case value belongs here.

profiles.description: A supplier's order confirmation or proforma invoice (PI).

fields.name: seller
fields.description: The selling party as labelled: the supplier confirming the order.

fields.name: buyer
fields.description: The buying party as labelled (PLX on a confirmation of a PLX purchase order).

fields.name: po_reference
fields.description: The purchase order the confirmation answers, as labelled (on a supplier's confirmation 'Customer PO' is PLX's PO).

profiles.description: A freight forwarder's quotation for a shipment.

fields.name: rate
fields.description: A price per rate-basis unit (per container, per CBM ...) as labelled ('Rate: USD 9,800'), never a total: operating/landed_cost.py plan_run multiplies it only by a cited count in containers for a container basis.

fields.name: basis
fields.description: The labelled rate basis line (per shipment, per 40HQ, per CBM ...), read only by operating/landed_cost.py plan_run, where an unreadable basis is unknown, never 'per shipment'.

fields.name: basis_count
fields.description: The count of the containers the quote is priced for, as labelled ('Containers: 1'), with the unit written next to it (container when none is written), folded by the extractor; a count in another unit (cbm, kg) is never a container count, one written with a unit the extractor does not read is a gap, and it is never inferred from the amount.

fields.name: volume
fields.description: The shipment volume the quote states ('Volume: 12.5 CBM'); the count of a per-CBM rate only in cbm, a gap when no unit is written.

fields.name: chargeable_weight
fields.description: The chargeable weight the quote states ('Chargeable weight: 1,200 kg'); the count of a per-kg rate only in kg (never converted, never the gross weight), a gap when no unit is written.

fields.name: pallet_count
fields.description: The count of the pallets the quote is priced for ('Pallets: 4'; pallet when no unit is written); the count of a per-pallet rate only in pallets.

fields.name: includes
fields.description: The labelled inclusions line (origin charges, main carriage, destination charges ...). A freight component counts as covered only when this line or the scope line names it.

fields.name: excludes
fields.description: The labelled exclusions line (duties and taxes, surcharges ...). A term operating/landed_cost.py does not recognise leaves the quote's scope unknown.

fields.name: seller
fields.description: The forwarder quoting, as labelled.

fields.name: buyer
fields.description: The party the quote is made to, as labelled.

fields.name: po_reference
fields.description: The purchase order the quote is for, as labelled.

profiles.description: A packing slip or packing list of a shipment.

fields.name: seller
fields.description: The shipping or selling party, as labelled.

fields.name: buyer
fields.description: The buying party, as labelled.

fields.name: po_reference
fields.description: The purchase order the shipment is packed against, as labelled.

profiles.description: A paper assembly order (AO) packet: the AO form, its shop-floor sheet and the finished-goods inspection / release sheet (scanned; read from the capture's OCR text when the PDF has no text layer).

fields.name: ao_lot
fields.description: The AO lot number as written (AO LOT#).

fields.name: bulk_lot
fields.description: The bulk batch lot as written (BULK LOT#); an AO lot is never a bulk lot.

fields.name: sales_order
fields.description: The sales order (OE) as written.

fields.name: customer_po
fields.description: The customer PO as written; often blank on the form.

fields.name: required_date
fields.description: REQUIRED DATE on the AO form.

fields.name: production_date
fields.description: The date the shop-floor sheet records production.

fields.name: qa_release_date
fields.description: The QA release date on the finished-goods inspection / release sheet.

fields.name: planned_quantity
fields.description: SIZE on the AO form: printed before committed, an estimate (Portal ManufacturingOrder.yieldExpected / FM qtymanufold meaning).

fields.name: produced_quantity
fields.description: Total QTY (EA) on the shop-floor sheet, labelled or as the QTY (EA) cell of its Total row (FM totalprodqty_c meaning); a bare Qty column's Total row (a component list's sum) is none.

fields.name: filled_quantity
fields.description: Quantity filled on the shop-floor sheet, labelled or as the QTY (EA) cell of its Filling row (a second Filling row with another quantity is a conflict, never a sum).

fields.name: retained_samples
fields.description: Samples (EA) / QC retain kept from the run (FM qtysample, Portal qtySample meaning), labelled or as the QTY (EA) cell of a Samples row.

fields.name: inspected_quantity
fields.description: A quantity the inspection sheet states as inspected; the sheet's header QUANTITY is not one.

fields.name: released_quantity
fields.description: A quantity the release sheet states as released (accepted; FM qtyacc_c meaning); a release tick is not one.

fields.name: rejected_quantity
fields.description: Rejects on the inspection sheet.

fields.name: damaged
fields.description: DAMAGES on the shop-floor sheet, keyed by component code.

fields.name: qc_checked
fields.description: QA/QC checked mark as written (initials, date); a document mark, not authenticated sign-off or release authority.

fields.name: shipment_released
fields.description: The SHIPMENT RELEASED box on the finished-goods release sheet; a document mark, never release authority.

fields.name: shipment_on_hold
fields.description: The SHIPMENT ON HOLD box on the finished-goods release sheet; a document mark, never a hold in any system.

profiles.description: A customer's purchase order to PLX: its PO number, dates, parties, shipping terms and line items. A purchase order PLX itself issued (to a supplier) is not one: the issuing party on the document or the file's provenance decides (not_issued_by_own_party); without either, the issuer is unknown (gap issuer_unknown).
A supplier's (commercial) invoice for goods PLX bought: its number, dates, the PO it names, amounts on their stated tax basis, shipping references and line items.
A bill of lading, waybill or freight invoice: the shipment's tracking reference, dates, parties, ports, packages, weights and freight charges.

A supplier's certificate of analysis (CoA) of one lot of a material: the product, lot, manufacture and expiry dates, the supplier, and the table of tests with each test's specification, result, unit and method as written. A machine-read lead: never a QC release, never a verified result.

fields.name: supplier
fields.description: The supplier or manufacturer issuing the certificate, as labelled.

fields.name: product
fields.description: The material the certificate is for, as labelled.

fields.name: product_code
fields.description: The supplier's code of the material, as labelled.

fields.name: lot
fields.description: The supplier's lot (batch) the results are for, as written; a supplier lot is never a PLX lot or receipt id: a lead to the receipt lines whose supplier lot it is, never to a PLX lab id or batch code.

fields.name: po_reference
fields.description: The PLX purchase order the certificate ships against, as labelled (a supplier's 'Customer PO' is PLX's PO); a lead to the PurchaseOrder, never proof the lot was received on it.

fields.name: expiry_date
fields.description: The expiry date the certificate states for the lot; a retest date is not one.

profiles.description: A delivery receipt or proof of delivery a carrier or consignee signed: when, to whom and how much was delivered, and in what condition.

fields.name: received_by
fields.description: The person who signed for the delivery, as written: personal data.

profiles.description: A document that records a decision about some record: an approval, release, sign-off, ruling or authorisation form (QC release of a batch or risk assessment, customer or QA approval of a proof, capitalisation or cost-policy approval, eligibility ruling, quote approval). Generic: what was decided is the document's own title, subject and outcome as written, who decided and when as written, and the basis the decider wrote; never a decision inferred from another record, and a blank signature, date or outcome is that field's gap (a form with empty approval fields records no decision).

fields.name: subject
fields.description: What the decision is about, as written.

fields.name: decision_type
fields.description: The kind of decision the document names, as written (its title is the class cue in evidence).

fields.name: outcome
fields.description: The decision as written (approved, rejected, released, on hold, eligible ...); a blank outcome is the gap, never an approval.

fields.name: decided_by
fields.description: Who made the decision, as written: personal data. A role written without a name is the role, never a person.

fields.name: signature
fields.description: The signature field as read: personal data; a blank signature is its gap, never a signed decision.

fields.name: decided_on
fields.description: When the decision was made, as written by its own label (approval, release, signature or decision date); a bare printed "Date:" on a form is no decision time.

fields.name: basis
fields.description: The basis the decider recorded, as written: the only basis of this decision; never inferred from another record.
